method: Official websites and public GitHub repository pages. Star counts are rounded observations, not exact API totals. Effort and caveats are implementation judgments.

sources.name: React Bits
sources.license: MIT + Commons Clause
sources.framework: React; JS/TS; CSS or Tailwind
sources.effort: Low for CSS; medium/high for WebGL
sources.caveat: MIT + Commons Clause permits use within applications, websites and products; it prohibits redistributing the components themselves. This gallery bundles eight actual components into demo applications, retains the license and links to the pinned upstream source. WebGL2 backgrounds need a fallback; the Tilted Card interaction is pointer-based.

sources.name: Magic UI
sources.license: MIT for public repo; Pro separate
sources.framework: React + Tailwind + Motion
sources.caveat: Strong marketing effects; combine selectively with quieter product controls.

sources.name: Paper Shaders
sources.license: Apache-2.0
sources.framework: Vanilla JS or React; WebGL
sources.caveat: README explicitly asks to pin dependency: breaking changes can occur under 0.0.x versions. Keep LICENSE/NOTICE when redistributing library code. Neuro Noise runs the actual 0.0.81 vanilla shader locally, with official preset values observed in the Paper customizer. WebGL2 is required; offscreen instances are disposed and global pause stops animation.

sources.name: Drei / React Three Fiber
sources.license: MIT
sources.framework: React + Three.js
sources.caveat: 3D foundation rather than drop-in DOM UI. Requires GPU, camera/light setup, asset work and fallback.

sources.name: tsParticles
sources.license: MIT
sources.framework: Vanilla plus React/Vue/Svelte/Angular and other adapters
sources.caveat: Load only required engine/plugins and reduce particle density on mobile.

sources.name: NES.css
sources.license: MIT
sources.framework: Plain CSS/SCSS; any frontend
sources.caveat: Provides components rather than page layout. Retro typography can reduce density/readability.

sources.name: 98.css
sources.license: MIT
sources.framework: Semantic HTML + CSS; any frontend
sources.caveat: CSS only: draggable windows and desktop behavior require separate JS.

sources.name: Neobrutalism Components
sources.license: MIT
sources.framework: React + Tailwind; based on shadcn/ui
sources.caveat: Opinionated thick borders and shadows can overwhelm dense dashboards.

sources.name: shadcn/ui
sources.license: MIT
sources.framework: React, Tailwind CSS; Base UI or Radix foundations
sources.caveat: Excellent functional baseline but visual distinction needs your own tokens. Accessibility still depends on composition.

sources.name: daisyUI
sources.license: MIT public library; paid products separate
sources.framework: Tailwind CSS; framework independent
sources.caveat: CSS classes provide styling; complex widget behavior still needs application code.

sources.name: Vaul
sources.license: MIT
sources.framework: React
sources.caveat: Actual Vaul 1.1.2 runs in the local drawer study. Upstream currently marks the project unmaintained; validate touch, scrolling and focus in your actual app.

sources.name: Rough.js
sources.license: MIT
sources.framework: Vanilla Canvas/SVG
sources.caveat: Drawing engine rather than accessible controls. Use semantic HTML for interaction and SVG for decorative treatment.

sources.name: Anime.js
sources.license: MIT public engine
sources.framework: Vanilla JS; adaptable to any frontend
sources.caveat: Animation engine requires composing your own components and cleaning up animations in framework lifecycles.

sources.name: css-doodle
sources.license: MIT component; public doodles MIT per current service terms
sources.framework: Web Component + CSS
sources.caveat: Large DOM grids can be expensive. Good for decorative surfaces, not functional widget primitives.

sources.name: Open Props
sources.license: License file exists; exact terms not verified in this pass
sources.framework: CSS custom properties
sources.caveat: Token foundation rather than a component collection.

sources.name: Uiverse
sources.license: Official site states all UI elements MIT
sources.framework: HTML/CSS and Tailwind snippets
sources.caveat: Community quality varies. Check each snippet's semantics, keyboard behavior and CSS isolation.

sources.name: Haikei
sources.license: Asset export rights not independently verified
sources.framework: SVG/PNG generator; any frontend
sources.caveat: Exported static assets, not animated interactive components.

sources.name: shadcn-svelte
sources.license: MIT
sources.framework: Svelte 5 + Tailwind + Bits UI
sources.caveat: Community-led port; use when Svelte is your implementation target.

sources.name: Vanta.js
sources.license: MIT
sources.framework: Vanilla JS; Three.js or p5.js; framework adapters by lifecycle integration
sources.caveat: Official site recommends at most one or two instances on a page, warns of slow WebGL on older devices and mobile incompatibility, and requires a fallback. This gallery uses actual Vanta with its documented older Three.js version isolated from modern Three.js demos. TOPOLOGY uses pinned p5.js 1.1.9 rather than WebGL; its 4,500 particle strokes form an autonomous flow field. The p5.js LGPL license is included in library notices.

sources.name: Souradip
sources.license: Inspiration only; original site footage, artwork and code are not licensed for redistribution
sources.framework: Observed: HTML chapter cards with two muted video elements; exact underlying stack not confirmed
sources.bestFor: Immersive portfolio storytelling with a distinctive crafted visual world
sources.caveat: Browser inspection found two video elements and no canvas. Scroll/click triggers cinematic chapter changes. Footage and illustration production, media loading, navigation and reduced motion are major implementation concerns. The local demo uses original real-time Three.js geometry, not the source’s videos or assets.
sources.visualInspection: Observed chapters 01 and 02, wheel/click transitions, camera travel and fading content cards; native browser DOM contained two muted video elements and zero canvases.

sources.name: Tabler Icons
sources.license: MIT
sources.framework: Plain SVG plus React, Vue, Svelte, Angular and other official packages
sources.bestFor: Consistent icons for navigation, actions, dashboards and product controls
sources.caveat: Use accessible labels on icon-only buttons; decorative icons should be hidden from assistive technology. Ship the icons you use instead of bundling the complete collection in a product.

sources.name: Lando Norris
sources.license: Inspiration only; source models, photography, branding and code are not licensed for reuse
sources.framework: Observed WebGL/canvas helmet interaction and Webflow-style DOM; exact animation implementation not confirmed
sources.bestFor: A distinctive interactive 3D product or personality hero
sources.caveat: Requires model/material production, hit testing or a reveal mask, pointer/touch handling, reduced motion and performance fallbacks. The local study uses original procedural geometry and a screen-space reveal shader.
sources.install: No component package; this is a bespoke website reference
sources.visualInspection: Observed ghost/wireframe helmet, coloured helmet patches revealed by pointer movement, pointer-dependent orientation, and tap-to-lock/back-to-scroll control. Tested default and desktop widths. Rendered DOM contained canvases and no videos.

sources.name: Animate UI
sources.framework: React, Tailwind CSS, Motion; Radix, Base UI or Headless UI primitives
sources.license: MIT + Commons Clause; application use allowed, original components cannot be sold or redistributed as a kit
sources.bestFor: Polished motion on familiar product UI patterns
sources.caveat: The local tabs demo uses actual source with original content. Retain the license; choose the matching primitive family for your application.

sources.name: Kibo UI
sources.framework: React + shadcn/ui; dependencies vary by component
sources.license: MIT for the public component source
sources.bestFor: Richer product interactions: comparison, kanban, Gantt, editors and colour picking
sources.caveat: Large components have additional dependencies. The local comparison demo uses actual Kibo source with a small keyboard adapter and original SVG artwork.

sources.name: tweakcn
sources.framework: Visual editor for Tailwind CSS and shadcn CSS tokens
sources.license: Apache-2.0 for the public editor source; exported presets are demonstrated with retained attribution
sources.bestFor: Compare real colour, radius, typography and shadow systems before implementation
sources.caveat: Local demo samples six actual theme token sets; it is not the full editor. Custom fonts use system fallbacks until you supply them.
sources.install: Export a theme from the official editor or install its provided registry URL

sources.name: coss ui
sources.framework: React, Base UI and Tailwind CSS
sources.license: Open-source component library; verify the exact component license and dependency terms before reuse
sources.bestFor: Refined product controls, composed input and chat composer patterns
sources.caveat: Origin UI now redirects to coss ui. Source reference only in this gallery; its components are not reproduced locally.

sources.name: ReUI
sources.framework: React, shadcn/ui and Tailwind CSS; data-grid dependencies vary
sources.license: Free component catalog plus separately paid Pro blocks; verify the terms of the selected item
sources.bestFor: Dense business UI: data grids, filters, schedules, kanban and application shells
sources.caveat: Free components and paid blocks have different scope. This is a linked source reference; no Pro block source is copied.
sources.install: Use the installation command on the selected free component page

sources.name: Design Prompts
sources.framework: Browser style explorer with full-page previews and AI design prompts
sources.license: Publicly accessible prompt gallery; a reuse license for site source code, photos and assets was not verified
sources.effort: Low for typography/layout exploration; implementation effort depends on the chosen treatment
sources.bestFor: Choose whole-page typography, colour and composition before selecting UI components
sources.caveat: Four original local compositions demonstrate Newsprint, Swiss Minimalist, Botanical and Maximalism. Full-page references remain linked. These are art-direction studies, not an upstream component library or copied prompts. Botanical uses original SVG illustrations. Some source light/dark labels differ from the observed preview appearance.
sources.install: Browse a style, inspect its full-page preview, then open Get Prompt

demos.name: Newsprint — editorial hierarchy and print-style layout
Swiss Minimalist — precise grids and strong type
Botanical — warm palettes and organic image framing

sources.inspection: Reviewed the 30-style list and visually inspected Monochrome, Industrial, Botanical, Newsprint, Swiss Minimalist, Academia, Organic, Maximalism and Retro. Shortlist is an editorial judgement.

sources.name: Impeccable
sources.license: See the upstream repository; local example markup and styles are original
sources.framework: Agent instructions; illustrative local HTML/CSS/JavaScript study
sources.bestFor: Refine an existing UI while preserving the chosen visual identity
sources.caveat: The local lab demonstrates selected guidance; it is not a complete skill workflow or measured benchmark. Upstream includes CLI tools and optional hooks.

sources.name: Taste Skill
sources.license: See the upstream repository; local example markup and styles are original
sources.framework: Agent instructions; illustrative local HTML/CSS/JavaScript study
sources.bestFor: Explore distinctive public-facing pages and creative sites
sources.caveat: The local lab shows selected v2 guidance only. Upstream has strict style bans, direction-draw scripts, imagery and motion floors, and an inspector; the full workflow was not executed.

sources.name: Awesome Design Skills
sources.license: See the upstream repository; local example markup and styles are original
sources.framework: Agent instructions; illustrative local HTML/CSS/JavaScript study
sources.bestFor: Choose a single style recipe before implementing a page
sources.caveat: The local demo selects the Editorial recipe. It does not represent all recipes or promise automatic quality improvements.
